answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging every new identity a registration toll in burned compute plus bonded stake, slashed if its work fails peer attestation. A thousand fakes must then pay that toll and post collateral for each persona, so the attacker's marginal cost scales with every identity while an honest operator amortizes a single bond across real tasks. Reputation is the crystal that hardens only through graded work, and vetted peers form a haven that declines to endorse unproven strangers, leaving raw ivory identities cold. Sybil swarms become too costly to sustain.
